scope: Authenticated bounded Unix-socket control server around the serialized radio controller. The runtime serve command does not yet bind this socket or instantiate a native radio coordinator.

validation.artifact_source: AArch64 debug test binary built from the clean implementation commit. Host tests used the identical source before commit. No packaged runtime image was built.

properties_exercised: Real Unix peer credentials and /proc process start times establish ownership. Requests cannot override UID/PID, choose executables/paths/units, or use unsupported schemas. The client rejects a server with the wrong UID before sending its request.

A separate exec of the Rust test binary cannot release a temporary hold owned by its parent process. A deployment capability admitted by a child remains releasable by the same account after that child exits.
Lost-response reservation retries do not allocate another hold. Renewal and idempotent release work, and replies do not echo the capability.
A request arriving through the real Unix socket during a blocked fake shutdown receives no admission until the coordinator restores the fake radio and reads back availability.

Expired queued work and mismatched process start identity cannot mutate policy. Stale generations cannot replace saved settings; corrupt persisted policy reports unavailable status and permits no radio write.

Eight incomplete clients occupy bounded workers; excess connections are rejected promptly and incomplete frames expire. A disconnected coordinator reports unavailable rather than transient queue pressure.

Both Pis ran the same checked test binary as UID 1000 with temporary state/socket paths and a fake radio backend. The subprocess fixture uses the Rust binary itself, without requiring Python on the device.
limits: serve does not bind the new network socket, and no native network actor or SSH admission hook is enabled in the runtime service.
Native SSH/session observation, the admission barrier, install guards, continuous NetworkManager change monitoring and expected setup profile changes still need integration.
The bootstrap access verifier currently rejects extra SSH ExecStartPre commands. The future hook and loaded-unit verifier must be updated together before image/bootstrap qualification.
The board fixtures use real Unix IPC and process credentials but fake radio/activity/guard observations. They do not qualify physical SSH/SCP/SFTP protection or live Wi-Fi shutdown.

One selected test is a subprocess fixture entry point, a no-op in the ordinary suite and exercised through child executions by the ownership case; the six parent cases provide the behavioral assertions.
No installed services, radio settings, credentials, data partitions, root/boot files or watchdog were modified. Boot IDs were unchanged within both runs.
Root connection details, supervised bootstrap, production signing/feed, downloader/install policy and full physical OTA qualification remain outstanding. The overall auto-update goal is incomplete.
